title: throughput-regression-continuous-batching-debug-scratchpad-14
content:
Scratchpad: throughput regression after config rollout - continuous batching

Summary:
- Observed throughput drop on hosted cluster (svc: chat-gen-prod) starting 2024-11-14 03:10 UTC after rolling out batcher config change (PR 987).
- Expected ~18-22k tokens/s aggregated, observed ~4-6k tokens/s at peak loads. Latency p95 jumped from ~80ms -> ~350ms for short prompts.
- Hypothesis: continuous batching window/config mismatch causing small batches to wait or fallback to single-request slow path; possibly interactions with KV cache invalidation or autoscaler downsizing.GPU utilization dropped from ~72% -> ~28% (same QPS).

Quick timeline / breadcrumbs:
- 2024-11-14 02:50 UTC: merged PR 987 (batcher: set default.window_ms -> 100, enable continuous_batching=true by default)
- 2024-11-14 03:05 UTC: canary rollout to 10% nodes
- 2024-11-14 03:10 UTC: metrics show throughput drop on canary hosts; rollback initiated to 0% at 03:22 UTC
- 2024-11-14 03:30 UTC: full rollback completed, throughput partially recovered but not fully to baseline
- 2024-11-14 04:00 UTC: opened INF-4321, started deeper investigation

Commands run (notes + outputs trimmed):
- Check recent deploy/manifests\
  kubectl -n redwood get deploy chat-gen-prod -o yaml | yq '.spec.template.spec.containers[0].env'
  -> saw REDWOOD_BATCHER_WINDOW_MS=100, REDWOOD_ENABLE_CONTINUOUS_BATCHING=true

- Tail logs on a canary host: 
  kubectl -n redwood logs -l role=batcher -c batcher --since=30m | grep -i "batcher" -A3 -B2 | tail -n 50\
  2024-11-14T03:08:51Z INFO  batcher: started window_ms=100 continuous=true
  2024-11-14T03:09:12Z WARN  batcher: backlog-exceeded, falling back to drain-now (backlog=14)
  2024-11-14T03:09:12Z INFO  batcher: issuing small batch drain: size=1 wait_ms=100
  2024-11-14T03:09:13Z DEBUG model-run: kv-cache-miss rate=0.42 (baseline 0.03)
  2024-11-14T03:09:13Z ERROR runtask: slow-path-execution duration_ms=1900 request_id=req-4f8a

- Extracted metrics via PromQL (Grafana):\
  sum(rate(model_tokens_generated[1m])) by (cluster) -> dropped by ~70% on canary cluster (03:09-03:20)
  95th(percentile(latency_ms[5m])) -> 350ms (was 75-90ms pre-rollout)
  batch_size_distribution -> spike in single-request batches (count at size=1 increased by 4x)

- Replayed load against canary host (local reproducer):\
  ./scripts/loadtest.py --target http://canary-host:8080/infer --concurrency 80 --seq-len 32 --duration 300\
  result summary: qps stable, but tokens/s per GPU dropped; CPU for batcher container high (~60%), GPU low (~25%)

Error snippets / interesting log lines:
- batcher: backlog-exceeded, falling back to drain-now
- model-run: kv-cache-miss rate=0.42 (baseline ~0.03)
- runtask: slow-path-execution duration_ms=1900 request_id=req-4f8a
- kernel-chooser: selected generic-kernel (quant path fallback) for model=redwood-small sequence=32

Observations / hypotheses:
- window_ms increased to 100ms caused more waiting, but we expected larger batch sizes -> should increase throughput. Instead, we see more single-request drains. Why?
  - Hypothesis A: continuous batching logic has a bug where backlog threshold check triggers fallback too aggressively when backlog metric is read stale. If backlog read reports small but real inflight is larger, code falls back incorrectly.
  - Hypothesis B: upstream autoscaler reduced number of serving replicas (scale-down) during rollout because of CPU-based metric threshold; fewer GPUs -> higher per-node queuing -> batcher falls back to drain-now to avoid head-of-line blocking, causing single request execution path.
  - Hypothesis C: KV cache invalidation bug: after deploy the KV cache warm-up is broken (kv-cache-miss spikes), so model run is slower (cache misses + kernel selection fallback), causing batcher to timeout waiting and flush small batches.
  - Hypothesis D: Recent kernel selection changes (PR 980) cause non-optimal kernel to be chosen for certain sequence lengths, reducing throughput by ~3-5x for small sequences. Logs show generic-kernel selected for many requests.

Quick diffs checked:
- PR 987 (batcher defaults) vs previous config: window_ms changed 8ms -> 100ms, backlog_threshold changed 16 -> 8 (really?). Need to confirm config conflation between 'backlog_threshold' and 'backlog_soft_limit' in configmap.
- PR 980 (kernel chooser) changed heuristics: prefer stable kernel if memory_pressure > 0.3. Memory_pressure reported from cgroup metrics; on canary hosts memory_pressure spiked due to sidecar injection (observability agent) -> may influence kernel selection.

Repro attempts and results:
- Reproduced locally with k8s minikube and injected sidecar -> saw kernel fallback + high batcher CPU. Throughput drop reproduced at ~70% of observed production regression, so not 1:1 but indicative.
- Forced REDWOOD_BATCHER_WINDOW_MS=8 on canary by patching deployment (not rollback) -> Observed throughput recovery to ~85% baseline within 90s.
  -> strong indicator that window_ms=100 is correlated but not definitive (could be compounding factors).
- Warmed KV cache before test (run synthetic warmup tool) -> improved latency by ~20% but still below baseline.

Immediate mitigations applied:
- Rolled back config to window_ms=8 (complete) -> partial recovery but some hosts still underperforming.
- Requeued some evicted pods to spread sidecar CPU load (kubelet restarted some pods)

Things to check / next steps (ordered):
1) Confirm configmap used by batcher pods at rollout time (timestamped): kubectl get cm redwood-batcher-config -o yaml --show-managed-fields | grep -A2 window_ms
2) Add logging around backlog metric read (trace numbers) to see if stale reads cause fallback. Short-term add debug flag in batcher to log backlog value and timestamp.
3) Check HPA / autoscaler events around 03:00-04:00 for scale-down reasons (metrics, cooldown). Investigate if scale-down was based on CPU metric that didn't account for queued work.
4) Re-run canary with sidecar disabled to isolate sidecar-memory-pressure effect; compare kernel chooser behavior.
5) Add temporary metric exposing kv-cache-hit-rate per model to validate hypothesis C.
6) Run synthetic reproducer with set of env toggles:
   - window_ms=8/20/50/100
   - continuous_batching=true/false
   - disable kernel-chooser heuristic (force optimized-kernel)
   Collect tokens/s, batch sizes, kv-cache-hit-rate, GPU utilization.
7) If confirmed bug in batcher fallback logic, raise hotfix PR to prevent aggressive fallback when backlog reads are older than X ms.

Notes for handoff to runtime team (what they need):
- Logs: canary host ids and exact timestamps (03:05-03:25 UTC). Attach logs.gz (already saved in /tmp/canary-logs-20241114.tar.gz).
- Reproducer: scripts/loadtest.py and scripts/warmup_kv.py in repo; use nodepool-canary-03 for best match.
- Config: redwood-batcher-config configmap version v12 (commit hash in CM annotations).
- Suspect PRs: PR 987 (batcher defaults), PR 980 (kernel chooser).

Open questions / unknowns:
- Why did rollback not fully restore baseline? (maybe persistent cache warming + nodes still running suboptimal kernel)
- Was there any correlated infra change (kubelet/OS update) on canary hosts at same time? Need host-level audit.
- Is there a race where batcher sees backlog decrease and flips to drain-now while more inflight requests are still hitting the model, causing head-of-line issues?

Action log (short):
- 2024-11-14 03:40 UTC: rolled back batcher config -> partial recovery
- 2024-11-14 05:10 UTC: reproduced locally + confirmed kernel chooser + sidecar interaction
- 2024-11-14 06:30 UTC: created this scratchpad + assigned follow-ups to Liam (trace logs) and Sofia (reproducer rigs)

Notes to self (random):
- If we add more logging, make it cheap (sample=0.01) to avoid adding noise in prod.
- Consider experiment: 2-phase rollout where window_ms is ramped (8 -> 20 -> 50) with telemetry gating.
- Check for similar regressions in dedicated clusters (customer impact) - open quick alert on #eng-runtime if confirmed.

Next update: add results of debug-logging and canary with sidecar-disabled.

-- Ava
